ai.summary: Backend dependencies updated to `ai@5.0.0` and `zod@4` (via `zod/v4` imports). Agent tool call interfaces migrated from `args` to `input` properties in `.agents/` definitions and `ToolCall` types. Zod error handling updated to use `error.issues` instead of `error.errors`. API max token parameters renamed from `maxTokens` to `maxOutputTokens` in `relabelRuns.ts`.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the assistant's internal plumbing was upgraded to newer core libraries, which required renaming how the assistant's built-in tools talk to each other. If you peek at the configuration files that define what the assistant can do, you'd see every command that used to be written with a field called 'args' is now written with a field called 'input', plus a few other minor adjustments to match the new tooling. This is live today and doesn't change what you experience, just keeps the foundation up to date and consistent.

ai.title: Improve agent import error message
ai.summary: Updated the verbose logging in `npm-app/src/agents/load-agents.ts` to print `error.name`, `error.message`, and `error.stack` directly instead of using `getErrorObject` from `@codebuff/common/util/error`. This change removes the dependency on the external error utility for this specific log, providing more granular stack trace details during local agent loading failures.

eli5.text: When a programmer adds a custom helper to this tool, and that helper has a mistake that stops it from loading, the error message now shows the exact name of the problem, the clear explanation, and the full step-by-step trail of where things went wrong, instead of a shortened generic note. Previously it bundled that information through a shared helper used across many places; now it reads the error straight from the source. You'd notice a longer, more detailed message only when a helper fails to load during development, and only if you had asked to see extra debugging information. This is live today for anyone building or testing custom helpers.
